label: Origin interface: each individual's origin at each world and a closeness relation on origins
definition: OriginInterface W B O supplies origin : W → B → O and near : O → O → Prop. W is the world carrier; B is the fixed candidate-individual carrier of Ontic; O is a supplied origin carrier, read as portions of originating matter. The same x : B denotes the same individual at each world. origin w x is semantically idle when x does not exist at w. near is a primitive closeness relation, intended to mean that origins differ within an admitted tolerance. The structure alone imposes no reflexivity, symmetry, metric, transitivity, access, existence or causal law. NearIsTolerance, OriginDeterminesAccess, OriginPlenitude and VariedOriginAt are separate explicit commitments, not fields proved by this dictionary.
note: Stipulative analyst interface for the existing finite controls, with attribution deferred. Reuses DEF-KANT-ONTOLOGICAL-MODEL and DEF-MODAL-FIXTURE-FRAME; DISAMB-COUNTERPART-VS-RIGID-IDENTITY distinguishes the fixed carrier from counterpart matching. In Control.interface the origin values are minus, actual and plus; adjacent offsets are near, opposite offsets are not. These offsets supply no physical measure of matter, kind-relative threshold, vagueness theory or historical attribution. Real material-origin interpretation, the closeness criterion and its applicability remain OPEN. Equal or near origins do not define individual identity, causal production, temporal persistence or existence. The motivating material-origin reading does not include a relation comparing kind or causal history; the arbitrary Lean origin carrier O does not itself exclude such an interpretation. Chandler/Salmon-style tolerance motivates this analyst interface but is not a verified attribution. Vagueness, kind-relative tolerance, counterpart readings and whether origin is the only essential constraint remain OPEN. The earlier NecessaryIf link defines box(G -> box G), not origin vocabulary.
